title: Workload Grokker: Continuous batching counsel + safe-apply
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build a lightweight runtime-side recommendation agent (the 'Workload Grokker') that analyzes per-customer request shapes and KV-cache effectiveness to suggest continuous batching and caching parameter adjustments. The Grokker produces conservative candidate configs (batch_size, max_duration_ms, prefix_cache_ttl, coalescing_window) and a safety plan for staged application including shadow-apply, canary, telemetry guards, and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Agent runs in analysis mode on live traffic snapshots and produces human-readable recommendations for >=90% of profiled workloads
Recommendations include estimated token-cost delta and 95th-p latency impact estimate
Safe-apply workflow implemented: shadow-apply -> canary (1% traffic) -> ramp with telemetry gates -> auto-rollback on safety signals
End-to-end integration test that simulates a workload spike and triggers rollback with configured thresholds
Dashboard card in Console showing recommended config, rationale, and confidence score
technical_notes: Profile features: median/95th seq len, request arrival distribution (lambda), response length distribution, KV cache hit ratio by prefix, hot-cold user splits
Heuristics engine uses prioritized rules: preserve p95 latency SLO first, then cost delta, then robustness to burstiness
Continuous tuner will propose delta adjustments (e.g., +10% batch_size) and recommend quantization-safe model variants where beneficial
Safety signals: p95 latency increase > 10% absolute or error rate increase > 0.5% triggers immediate rollback
Telemetry: use existing per-route token breakdowns + new 'grokker-reason' span tags for traceability
Config schema: flat keys (batch.size, batch.max_wait_ms, cache.prefix_ttl_ms, coalesce.window_ms) plus metadata (confidence, sample_ids)
